title: RAW UNREVIEWED: viewing context changes a prescribed measure while actual thickness stays distinct from appearance
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Complete cached Vitruvius III.3.11 links spacing, actual shaft thickness and apparent slenderness, then prescribes a corner-column enlargement by one fiftieth of its own diameter. A globally reused fraction/reference construction must supply the correction's base and later physical dimension; an appearance predicate must retain its viewing context. This is a contextual proportion argument, not a material transformation or actor-state machine. No target values are assigned.

design.author_role: bounded independent idea producer; root owns selection
design.whole_content_hypothesis: A short design argument first establishes dimensions relative to one written standard, distinguishes actual measure from appearance in a viewing context, and uses the appearance discrepancy to prescribe a modified measure. Repeated short fraction/comparison/reference grammar constrains the resulting dimension rather than assigning an unrelated value to each stage. Literal architecture is a paid content hypothesis, not an observed manuscript genre.

source.work: Vitruvius De architectura, complete III.3.11; entire III.3.1–13 and VI.2.1–5 read as context
source.edition: Morgan1914 English translation of the ancient work, cached from Project Gutenberg20239. No Latin/diplomatic medieval witness was collated; no native source image or new acquisition.
source.focal_content: In wide araeostyle spacing, a ninth/tenth height fraction makes shafts look thin; in narrow pycnostyle spacing, an eighth makes them look swollen. The author therefore requires style-appropriate proportions. Corner columns should be thicker than the others by a fiftieth of their own diameter because the unobstructed outline makes them seem more slender. The conclusion explicitly presents adjusted proportions as compensation for ocular deception.
source.complete_context: III.3 defines five spacing classes and gives intercolumniation, module, shaft-height and diameter relations before the focal paragraph. Sections12–13 give the complete height-dependent top-diminution cases and their visual rationale. VI.2 distinguishes measured symmetry from appearance, includes flat scenery and a straight oar appearing broken in water, and allows additions/diminutions suited to site. It leaves the optical explanation open between image-impact and rays from the eye; this RAW imports neither theory as settled.
source.complete_unit_limit: The offered bounded argument is the entire paragraph11, not an isolated fiftieth phrase and not a claimed whole-work translation. Every clause of that paragraph remains owed. Previous style/dimension declarations are explicit prerequisites if used; following diminution rules and the promised entasis figure/calculation are not silently part of its corner rule. The promised figure/calculation was not inspected.
source.historical_claim_ceiling: The proportions and perceptual rationale are historical assertions/prescriptions. No actual controlled paired observation, correct optical mechanism, numerical equality of perceived sizes or successful construction is established. No Voynich source dependence, dating, locality or confirmed architectural word follows.

Paragraph pins include each complete p element without newline normalization. Reading stripped HTML tags and decoded entities for display only; original bytes were not changed.

proposed_common_language_obligations.objects: A shaft x, a positive measured height H, a diameter measure D and a written style/viewing context C. A corner role is a geometric/location condition, not a new material state or a second actor. If different shafts are compared their identities and common standard must be explicit; the source does not supply one physically observed object moved between contexts.
proposed_common_language_obligations.fraction_grammar: One FRACTION(base,numerator,denominator) operation produces a quantity of the same dimension as its written base. MEASURE(x,thickness) and APPEARS(x,thickness-description,C) are distinct predications. An ADD_DIMENSION construction may consume a derived fraction and original dimension; it cannot accept a bare property label in place of a quantity. No source number is assigned to an EVA/BPE part.
proposed_common_language_obligations.comparison_grammar: Actual diameter comparisons retain the specified physical quantities; apparent slenderness retains the observer/site/style context. A repeated thickness root can serve both only through an explicit common property and different predication constructors, not a whole-word exception at every occurrence. No automatic invisible switch of context is licensed.
proposed_common_language_obligations.corner_rule: The corner prescription consumes the same diameter reference used by its fraction. The writer must declare whether own diameter denotes the uncorrected design diameter or the corrected resulting diameter. The source translation is not used to certify one mathematical referent. Both interpretations remain visible before target authoring; a later selector cannot choose whichever matches the target.
proposed_common_language_obligations.source_sized_debts: All focal spacing examples, inappropriate fractions, style-appropriate requirement, corner relation, comparison with other columns, reason and adjustment conclusion remain part of the whole proposed P5 account. Any use of chapter10's dimension rules must supply its written height/style/base arguments. No short fraction formula is offered as the whole62-group reading, and no clause may become a padding label.

linked_consequences.steps: Bind H and a style context; apply the source's declared base-diameter proportion in the same fraction grammar; then carry that result into the physical comparison or corner-correction expression.
linked_consequences.result: For the paid paired example with common positive H, araeostyle D=H/8 and pycnostyle D=H/10 imply D_araeostyle/D_pycnostyle=5/4. A later expression consuming D cannot keep one shared absolute diameter while retaining those written bindings. This is derived from the source ratios plus an explicitly added common-H comparison, not a recorded pair of measured buildings.
linked_consequences.decision: A whole C0 account that actually reuses a computed diameter in a later written construction gains a concrete dependency beyond naming two styles. An account that simply supplies unrelated quantities at the later site does not satisfy this proposed shared grammar; stop lexical growth rather than repair the result.

linked_consequences.steps: Bind the physical comparison to another/uncorrected diameter D and bind the one-fiftieth expression to its declared own-diameter referent; then require the later corrected dimension to consume that exact result.
linked_consequences.result: With BASE_REFERENCE fixed in advance, D_corner=D+D/50=51D/50. With FINAL_REFERENCE fixed in advance, D_corner=D+D_corner/50=50D/49. These are two paid interpretations of the English reference, not two source-attested measurement outcomes. A common fraction/reference construction must choose consistently, and the corrected quantity must remain physically larger in either version for D>0.
linked_consequences.decision: A frozen construction that changes its fraction base by occurrence, substitutes an absolute increment, or leaves the later dimension independent fails this explicit content contract. If the written reference remains unbound, retain both readings and do not start a quantitative decoder.

linked_consequences.steps: Keep actual thickness and the context-qualified appearance in separate predication frames; connect the corner appearance discrepancy to the stated correction prescription.
linked_consequences.result: Apparent slenderness does not assert a physical loss of diameter, and prescribed enlargement does not assert that the object first became thinner. A purely intrinsic-thinness reading would need an additional real diminution event absent from this declared argument. The source supplies no exact equality of corrected perceived sizes, so the account must not derive one.
linked_consequences.decision: Preserve the appearance/measure distinction if a whole written grammar expresses it and uses the quantity downstream. If the distinction is supplied solely by the author from an imagined scene, the contextual appearance route remains unselected.

strong_rivals.survival: A style-specific unary function directly supplies D(H), and a separate named CORNER_UPLIFT(D) supplies the same corrected measure. It can preserve all arithmetic without a productive context argument or an independently identified appearance predicate. The present source does not by itself exclude this representation.

strong_rivals.survival: Jointly rename column/diameter/style/viewer as an object/extent/context/display system, retaining its comparative bias and corrective prescription. It preserves every declared type, dependency and numeric result. A C0 pass cannot uniquely select architecture or literal perception.

strong_rivals.name: absolute additive increment
strong_rivals.difference: A fixed extra length can match one chosen D but fails the same fraction rule when another written base changes. A second actual written base would be needed before claiming productive proportionality; no held target or manufactured second source observation is supplied.

strong_rivals.name: intrinsic physical thinning
strong_rivals.difference: Treat the source appearance as a measured decrease and correction as restoration. That requires a separately written diminution event or qualified scope, rather than turning unobstructed air into an unstated material-removal operation.
